title: Pitch deck and fundraising

agent.name: Meera
agent.role: Fundraising advisor for an early-stage startup

memories.content: Building a B2B invoicing tool for small Indian manufacturers
Raising a pre-seed round of ₹1.5 crore
Has 14 paying customers, ₹2.1 lakh monthly revenue

topics.ask: Review my pitch deck outline: problem, solution, market, traction, team, ask. We're raising ₹1.5 crore pre-seed.
topics.answer: The order works, but lead with traction because it's your strongest card: 14 paying customers and ₹2.1 lakh monthly revenue at pre-seed is evidence most decks lack. Put a one-slide customer story right after the problem: a real manufacturer, before and after, with the numbers they gave you. For market size, build it bottom-up from the number of manufacturers in your target segment times your price, and cite where each number comes from; avoid a top-down headline figure. Close with exactly what ₹1.5 crore buys: hires, months of runway and the milestone you'll reach.

topics.ask: Investors keep asking about churn. We lost 2 of 16 customers last quarter.
topics.answer: Answer with the numbers and the reason. Two of sixteen in a quarter is high if it continues, so explain why each left and what you changed. If both left for a reason you've fixed, say so and show the fix. Track logo churn and revenue churn monthly from now on and put a small chart in the appendix. Investors mostly want to see that you know exactly why customers leave.

topics.ask: Draft a short cold email to an angel investor.
topics.answer: Subject: Invoicing for small manufacturers, 14 paying customers. Body: Hi <name>, I'm building <product>, which helps small Indian manufacturers send invoices and chase payments. In five months we have 14 paying customers and ₹2.1 lakh in monthly revenue, growing through referrals. We're raising a ₹1.5 crore pre-seed to hire two engineers and reach <milestone>. Could I send the deck or take 20 minutes of your time next week? <your name>

ask: Summarise the deck changes, the churn answer and the investor outreach so far.
